reviews.text: Lowery's ability to represent dark and medieval fantasy in an original visual way, while adding to the deconstruction of the hero's journey, gives a sense of power to the film. Patel was the perfect choice. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: The Green Knight is a cinema experience like few others.
reviews.author: Zach Youngs

reviews.text: “The Green Knight” has a magnificent cast and is visually stunning. If it was a silent film, I may have enjoyed it more.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: Possibly the most beautiful, and near inscrutable film this year, is David Lowery's epic, Arthurian tale. In a film world full of obvious explanations, The Green Knight provides precious few.
reviews.author: Dave Giannini

reviews.text: The performances are second to none, the plot is interesting and the surreal medieval feel is nothing short of an experience. The cinematography is the movies shining star, with memorable shots creating a visionary spectacle.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: Spellbound journey that had me in a hauntingly beautiful trance the entire way through. Bleak, Bold, Brilliant, & downright thought provoking.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Andrew Droz Palermo's stunning cinematography, Daniel Hart's atmosphere-setting score, and especially Johnny Marshall's impactful sound design deeply elevate the tremendous epic scope that this movie holds.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: The beauty of nature captured by carefully constructed camera work with poignant editing can only last so long.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: The Green Knight is astounding. It’s a magical experience of looking at the modern view of the dramatization of Gawain, regardless of whether they are a few changes from the original poem.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: Overall, The Green Knight’s impactful imagery and intensity outweigh its sometimes overly cryptic metaphors, allowing for quality entertainment.
reviews.author: Peter Bell

reviews.text: Of all the quality films released in 2021, none delivered a sense of awe for me as a viewer quite like David Lowery’s latest.
reviews.author: Brett Doze

reviews.text: The retelling of Welsh lore marries the core draw of the fantasy genre with themes of religion, morality, and chivalry in a grand epic hoping to soothe the burns left behind by Game of Thrones.
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: It’s got one of the best 4K releases of the year, which enhances the gorgeous cinematography, the rich sound design, and the ethereal score that permeates the film.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wiebe

reviews.text: The Green Knight is not for the faint of heart. Its methodical pacing will challenge viewers, but its execution will warrant cinephiles accepting that challenge. As a result, it’s one of Lowery’s best films and one of the best films of 2021.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: The Green Knight is a mesmerizing and marvelously crafted masterwork from director David Lowery, who effortlessly enlivens the Arthurian legend of yore.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: I will always argue that the screen is a very different medium from the page, and that film should be judged as a different medium, but this film version fails...
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: David Lowery uses every ounce of his creative freedom to make something audacious, challenging, and unlike any Arthurian adaptation we’ve seen to date.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Lowery wholeheartedly dives into the legend. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Inspired by 80s fantasy films Willow and Excalibur, a tale that risked being stodgy and inaccessible becomes enthralling thanks to its captivating visuals.  In Gawain, Patel brings us a medieval hero who feels human.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: The Green Knight thrives with its intrigue and suspense.
reviews.author: Britany Murphy

reviews.text: The Green Knight is ultimately a mixed bag.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: The Green Knight plays like conceptual art stretched over a narrative faade. Its themes feel grossly underserviced by a production too concerned with appearances, which is a shame given the potential of both the sights and ideas behind them.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Green Knight is Lowerys most accomplished work and one of the greatest cinematic Arthurian adaptations there has ever been.
reviews.author: Christopher Cross

reviews.text: Director David Lowery delivered something that was visually stunning and powerful, yet still felt fresh. A new kind of hero’s story.
reviews.author: Kevin Fallon

reviews.text: Another haunting and profound enchantment from David Lowery.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: I have wondered when we were going to collectively wake up and realize how good Dev Patel really is. The casting here is perfect, as Patel's persona practically radiates aspirational nobility.
reviews.author: Kenneth R. Morefield

reviews.text: The Green Knight diverges like a dream teetering toward a nightmare. But it also remains deeply relatable...
reviews.author: Vinnie Mancuso

reviews.text: As in most good tales of this kind, the quest itself-hunting down the legendary Green Knight for what looks like a certainly doomed matching of swords-is somewhat beside the point.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: David Lowery's bold, singular adaptation of a classic text bleeds atmosphere and imagination from every pore.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: Lowery's Arthurian fantasy, beyond its symbolic truism with aesthetic pretensions, seems to me infinitely dull and lacking in narrative impulse. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: In the hands of writer-director David Lowery, this classic Arthurian tale becomes a modern meditation on, well, everything.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: The few things I did see in a cinema weren't always the most scintillating. The Green Knight, despite being art directed, was something of a headscratcher. As in: who is this for, exactly?
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: Always one to re-examine myths from a new perspective, this adaptation of the 14th-century poem "Sir Gawain and the Green Knight" finds writer-director-editor David Lowery looking at legends that formed around medieval knights.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: That climatic part of the narrative is... the perfect ending to a classic fable full of mysticism. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sofía Alvarez Salas

reviews.text: [Contains] difficult balance between the brutal and the poetic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: [Patel's] soulful eyes, unruly mane and magnetic charm the camera merrily drinks in. As he charts Gawain's journey from brash naivety to tempered maturity, it is hard to mistake the sense of an epic unfolding on screen.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: This movie is a visual poem. It's the kind of thing that reminds me why I go to theaters, and why I love film.
reviews.author: Leah Schnelbach

reviews.text: At its center is a performance from Patel that walks the knife's edge between folly and vigor, between wisdom and lamentation, and between predetermination and doubt.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: Lowery's elusive adaptation withholds its meaning up to and beyond that final image of a mossy stump. It's left to the viewer to puzzle out the ending for herself on the way home -- an invitation to another most excellent adventure.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Sprawling, strange and dreamlike, David Lowery's interpretation of Arthurian legend is ripe for our time, and Dev Patel is excellent as the headstrong Gawain.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: The Green Knight is an enthralling morality tale possessing a profound lyrical beauty that is all its own. It is an intoxicating brew of wild fantasy and high-art that will stupefy your senses, leaving you lucid dazed under its hallucinatory spell.
reviews.author: Hasitha Fernando

reviews.text: Anyone who's followed Lowery's career won't be surprised to see how skilfully everything comes together... but this still feels like a big, bold new step for the director.
reviews.author: Paul M. Bradshaw

reviews.text: Its calculated contradictions make it a wondrously impossible film, so richly confounding, so truly hypnotic, so gorgeous to the eye, one is tempted to immediately rewatch it.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: The movie's modern, slyly deflationary approach to its material has as much to do with that classic film of antiheroism, Monty Python and the Holy Grail, as it does with high Arthurian legend.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: The Green Knight is a breathtaking, bold and beautiful Arthurian epic from director David Lowery, anchored by a tortured star turn from Dev Patel.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: The Green Knight is an astounding film, rich in its visuals, its storytelling, and its themes.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: This is a decidedly unique fantasy epic that deserves to be experienced on the biggest screen possible. It also confirms David Lowery as a major talent, and it will be fascinating to see what he does next.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: Though the action of The Green Knight never slows, Lowery leaves room for reflection. He favors a long take, a refreshing choice in a cinematic moment obsessed with speed.
reviews.author: Will DiGravio

reviews.text: It's Dev Patel summer, and it's a hot one thanks in part to his turn as Sir Gawain in The Green Knight.
reviews.author: Pablo Gallaga

reviews.text: It's a pity that the preceding two hours don't always fit, either thematically or qualitatively, with this dramatic, meaningful denouement.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: This slow-burn fantasy is exceptionally gorgeous with memorable imagery but heavy on cryptic symbolism.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: It might have been too much, too heavy, were it not for Patel. He is sympathetic in every frame... here he has graduated to something more commanding. He now has the gravitas of a leading man and radiates movie-star charisma.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: The Green Knight's attempts to blend a young man's personal reckonings and psychic confrontations with Lowery's go-for-broke stylings feel less virtuously enigmatic than flat and disjointed in their opaque graspings at profundity.
reviews.author: Beatrice Loayza

reviews.text: Knight is ultimately a tale of honor though, and a deeply moral one -- inscrutable, but haunting too.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: The exceptional level of craftsmanship -- which includes some seamless, low-key special effects -- wouldn't be nearly as affecting without the comparable care Lowery brings to this story.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: While you couldn't call The Green Knight a "faithful" adaptation of the poem, it might be a more faithful adaptation of the bigger legend around Gawain's adventure than a line-by-line recreation ever could have been.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: It's gorgeous, filled with breathtaking performances, and takes on Arthurian Legend like we haven't seen before, especially in a film as anticipated as this one.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: An adventure in search of honor that's too dry and cryptic at times, but in which the actor Dev Patel achieves one of his best performances to date. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: Sculptural minimalism defines the medieval stonework, clanking armour takes on the sleek, supple forms of fetishwear, light piercing the frame from unnatural places, sometimes saturating entire scenes in acid baths of verdigris green and radium yellow.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: David Lowery took an ancient myth and dressed it up in glorious, fairy tale finery.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: There is a sense, then, in which we have all entered into a deal with a proverbial Green Knight -- and we mustn't flinch from the knowledge that whatever blows we deal to him, will in due course be dealt back to us.
reviews.author: Keva York

reviews.text: A profound moviegoing experience unlike any other.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: It's a film that will enthral and fascinate audiences who won't be able to push it - and certain images - out of their heads.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: This is a slow-moving movie (125-minutes) that will make you think, during and after. By the end I was comparing it with the work of Danish director Lars von Trier...
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: The Green Knight is an elegant slow-burn, but it rewards the attentive viewer in spades.
reviews.author: George Fenwick

reviews.text: An epic quest designed to take the viewer on as much of a journey as its protagonist and leave you with plenty to ponder as the end credits roll.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Even if you're familiar with the lore, it may prove maddeningly oblique. Best not to get too hung up on plot and just roll with the vibe.
reviews.author: Tony Stamp

reviews.text: Over-calculated as it is, The Green Knight does have its authentically dreamlike passages. Near the heart of everything is the hero's ambivalent, perhaps masochistic sexuality.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: The Green Knight is, in essence, a return to Camelot's faerie roots... forcing us to believe in magic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yago García

reviews.text: Brilliantly composed in modern form, Lowery has made a tight sweeping epic wherein every frame could be hung upon a wall as decoration, where the poetry of the tale is made flesh, and the resonance of the message transcends time and space.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Weird but a fascinating fantasy trip.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: It's a fascinating and jarring experience from beginning to end and everything about it from the cinematography to the score is special.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: The filmmakers hope that their extreme style and slow-moving camera will distract from the fact that their college essay has a mediocre thesis.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: As intriguing as it is challenging, The Green Knight excels as a hallucinatory cinematic puzzle that will scramble your brain in the best possible way.
reviews.author: Ann Lee

reviews.text: The Green Knight is epic, gorgeous, philosophical, existential and at times obscure.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: In this majestic setting, heavy with symbolic imagery, Lowery brings Gawain's tale to a conclusion seven centuries in the making. It's a daring piece of work, and an invitation to step out of the circle, to walk a new path, to write our own story afresh.
reviews.author: Jennie Kermode

reviews.text: This is a gorgeous story about self-discovery, laced with ribald humour and fascinating details.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Fittingly for a story that is often opaque, the action plays out in muddy light or at arm's length: this is a movie to be squinted at as much as watched.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: A tale told mainly via startling visuals requires an actor with a singularly expressive face, and Patel rises to the challenge. He strips away knightly courage to reveal the fear lurking behind every so-called 'hero'.
reviews.author: David Hughes

reviews.text: The Green Knight becomes a distinct, virtuous warning, in a world of wannabe influencers to not kill yourself to become a story others' tell.
reviews.author: Diandra Reviews

reviews.text: The Green Knight is a trip in every sense of the word: an odyssey into the unknown that revels in its strangeness at every turn. They don't make 'em like this anymore.
reviews.author: Phil W. Bayles

reviews.text: [Lowey] returns to form with The Green Knight, a good-looking, nicely acted but somewhat embroidered retelling of the medieval tale of Sir Gawain...
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: The Green Knight is far from the most faithful adaptation ever put to screen - in fact, it may be up there with Monty Python in terms of Arthurian accuracy - but its deviations and amendments are always far from uninteresting.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: Superbly executed, marvellously strange, freighted with portent and utterly boring, all at the same time.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: What a strange and peculiarly powerful film this is.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: A bold, gorgeous and darkly comic cautionary tale about the making of legends, and heroes who don't even own their own story.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: What ultimately puts The Green Knight beyond the pale, for me, is the posthumanism of Lady Bertilak's monologue and how her speech helps to shape and determine the meaning of the ending in what I can only consider a nihilistic direction.
reviews.author: Steven D. Greydanus

reviews.text: A gorgeous, earthy movie which knows exactly when to tend towards the psychedelic.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: ...the best version of this story since the 14th century....
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: An unabashedly complex art film that is never watered down or affected by the fear of of box office failure. Simply stunning.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Lowery has taken the source material and made something exalted from it. The Green Knight is weird, wonderful, and genuinely superb.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Patel... seems to be growing as an actor before our eyes.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: A visual feast that lingers long after the end credits.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Writer-director David Lowery...turns Arthurian legend on its head in The Green Knight to deliver an intoxicating fantasy adventure which grapples with ideas rarely seen in this genre.
reviews.author: Andrew Murray

reviews.text: These moral explorations are carefully handled, with clever inversions of timeline that produce just enough of a puzzle quality to give the viewer something to work out when leaving the theater. But the movie enthralled me most in its visual meditations.
reviews.author: Kathryn Reklis

reviews.text: The Green Knight has bottled that feeling of ancient foreboding - it's Arthurian legend at its most rich and enigmatic.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Seek it out. Make the journey. You won't regret it.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: If you see the movie passing, salute it - a fearless if possibly foolhardy genre of one.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: A rivetingly weird and exceptionally beautiful fantasy film that offers no easy answers but ponders the biggest questions - through myths, mysticism, and men in crisis. This is major stuff from David Lowery.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: Monty Python and the Holy Grail is sometimes waggishly described as Ingmar Bergman with more laughs. By the same token, The Green Knight is a bit like Monty Python and the Holy Grail without them.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Also lovely to behold is Dev Patel's striking performance. His Gawain might be a naive mama's boy, but the knight-to-be is also an immensely likeable and relatable narrator of this weird tale.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: An abstract, nightmarish interrogation of chivalric honour and the karmic cost of bolstering one's own legend.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: In lieu of hero-buildling and stylized violence, David Lowery's take on Arthurian legend invites you to soak in its vibes and chew the scenery.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: The film's haunting imagery is hard to shake and the freshness it brings to the medieval adventure flick shows appropriate amounts of courage.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Lowery's The Green Knight is the kind of movie that will leave you thinking long after the credits roll and it's all the better for that. It may not be for everyone, but it's a brutal journey, beautifully crafted with stellar performances.
reviews.author: Amanda the Jedi

reviews.text: This is [Dev Patel's] film all the way.
reviews.author: Saibal Chatterjee

reviews.text: A romantic fantasy so overwhelming it leaves you shivering in awe of cinema's possibilities.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: Gawain is a deeply flawed man who is struggling to find a path for himself and Patel captures this internal strife with a confidence that is marvelous to see.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Treading across fantasy, adventure, human nature, and existential dread, The Green Knight has some stunning and breathtaking 'must-watch' moments. What it fails to be however, is the greatest sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Aniruddho Chakraborty

reviews.text: A glorious spiritual adaptation of the idea at the centre of the text.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: The Green Knight shows there's more here than a period piece swathed in arthouse stylings.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: ... fantastically filmed, exerting a strange power of fascination.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: The Green Knight rewards viewers' patience and stick with you long after the credits roll, particularly for those who are game to divine a greater meaning from its enigmatic offerings.
reviews.author: Hannah Lodge

reviews.text: An ethereal spectacle; part Tarkovsky, part Herzog, a surreal morality play that feels at once ancient and contemporary, a myth spun out of time.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: [The Green Knight] is as haunted as any horror movie artifact, be it a killer VHS tape or a cabin in the woods. It's not a matter of frights here -- the film just leaves you with feelings you can't put names to even days later.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: Easily one of the best pictures of the year, The Green Knight is an eerie and enchanted fantasy epic based on -- of all things -- an anonymous 14th-century poem with links to Christian mythology and Arthurian legend.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: A feminist retelling of a pagan fable, a deconstruction of masculinity, and a revisionist take on the hero's journey, The Green Knight is among the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Well-executed fantasy adventure film for adults set in Wales.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: I find the narrative to be unnecessarily confusing. Going from dream, to reality, back to dreams without any clarification is baffling and certain choices don't make any sense
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: David Lowery has delivered a film that's hallucinogenic, sensual, and spiritual.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: The film is impeccable, with a very well told story and very good performances. The cinematography of The Green Knight is impressive, with fabulous photography. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alvaro Corujo

reviews.text: The Green Knight wants to be a complex allegory of the death drive, but fails to touch on its own narrative's chivalric code or the inherent dark humor at its core.
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: It is one of bold vision, remarkable cinematic skill, and confident artistry.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Can't bridge the gap between its lush images and the emotional context behind them. The resulting film purports to be a slow-moving and existential affair, but can't seem to face the fact that it isn't as deep or sorrowful as it deems itself to be.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: It's a visually seductive, often-entrancing piece that wants you to meditate on its metaphors. It's also quite slow-paced and hypnotic, so much so that it may tempt you into closing your eyes and drifting off for a bit.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: David Lowery's interpretation of the classical poem of Sir Gawain and the Green Knight is a mass of contradictions: modern and primeval, a simple parable pregnant with hidden meaning, literary but also profoundly cinematic.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: What Lowery does in The Green Knight is make time tangible, anchoring this legend in a modern context.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Dark, moody and murky the movie plods along on a surreal adventure that lacks real entertainment value.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: A24 delivers once again with a haunting and challenging deconstruction of the hero's journey.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: A soft, still dawning world drawn with a palette of forest and fog, dun and peat, droplets, mist and motes. [S]erene, confident pacing accommodates the atmospheric possibilities [of] built environments of videogames like Death Stranding.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: A visually stunning film that I admire more than love.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: If the old ideas of chivalry, romanticism and honor remain in our society, they are greatly weakened. Karma is a nice idea, but life seldom works out that way. So this story seems irrelevant. It is more of an exercise in form.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: David Lowery's riff on Arthurian legend is full of profound truth and awe-inspiring spectacle, but its grayscale world is as opaque as it is impressive.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: I cheer on Lowery's luminous time-traveling. Pure cinema poetry.
reviews.author: Gerald Peary

reviews.text: The result is a spellbinding, and breathtakingly bold, cinematic experience.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: Each time Lowery shows a strange or striking image - a skull that turns into a talking head or a blind woman silently observing a seduction -- it fades away without having any lasting impact.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Edalatpour

reviews.text: Not since John Boorman's Excalibur has there been such a visually stunning and enchanting tale based on King Arthur mythology. David Lowery's monumental achievement.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Look at it as a Daniel Lanois production, swampy and mysterious, with echoes of the old and weird but not quite the real thing.
reviews.author: Sean Gilman

reviews.text: If you've ever wondered what constitutes "a critic's film," look no further than The Green Knight.
reviews.author: Alicja Johnson

reviews.text: That rascal finally made a great film.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: All the elements work together to create a singular, oneiric experience - one unlikely to be matched this or any other year.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: I'd be lying if I said I did not smile when I discovered what the director is ultimately up to here.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: David Lowery's retelling of "Sir Gawain and the Green Knight" deserves to be praised as one of the best fantasy films ever made.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: English majors will love what director David Lowery has done with "The Green Knight." The rest of us? Not so much.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: This is a frequently beautiful movie, albeit one set in a dark, damp, distant past that is brutish even when fantastical; slowly paced by current standards, yet never unengaging.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Dev Patel is compelling in visual storyteller David Lowery's enchanting chivalric romance.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: An impeccable medieval epic that leads us through an introspective journey about man's desire to transcend and achieve greatness. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: David Lowery has created a darkly brooding, atmospheric fantasy quest that is as richly textured and layered as the 14th century medieval poem on which it is based.
reviews.author: Jennifer Ouellette

reviews.text: I was not really prepared for what "The Green Knight" had in store so I let the tale wash over me. It is an intriguing story not of bravery but of finding that bravery and living a chivalric life of honor.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: The cast is so good it becomes extremely frustrating to watch Lowry pull out way too many bells and whistles visually. It's as if Lowry the director doesn't trust his cast so he tries to distract the audience by over-emphasizing the camera work.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: The film is a visual tour de force thanks to the splendid cinematography of Andrew Droz Palermo, the costumes by Malgosia Turnsganza and the production design of Jade Healy.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: Dev Patel shines in this bold, unorthodox Arthurian legend adaptation. David Lowery makes a visual poetry with imaginative camera work, atmospheric tone + gorgeous production design. but in the end, the film didn't cast a magical spell on me.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: [The Green Knight] was a sumptuous visual feast, an aesthetic wonder...beautiful to look at, compelling and chilling, bringing forth a sense of grounded fantasy that isn't quite like anything I've seen before.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: It's definitely not for everyone -- despite its dramatic title, it's anything but superhero fare -- but it's also precisely the sort of jolt the summer onslaught of films, depressingly craven up to this point, so badly needs.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: David Lowery's mesmerizing adaptation of the 14th-century poem of Arthurian legend is a deliriously sumptuous -- if, at times, impenetrable -- rendering of an early "Hero's Journey" that is a delight as long as you're willing to work with it.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: David Lowery's film is the kind that makes one reconnect with their love of the movies; an artform of grandeur & spectacle that can transport us into our own being to examine who we want to see in the mirror and on screen. Extraordinary filmmaking!
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Pacing, velocity, and flow don't interest Lowery. He knows the effects he wants and, skilled as he is, knows how to get them. But are they worth getting?
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: In a summer of junk, cinema visionary David Lowery delivers a modern movie masterpiece about a wannabe knight (an Oscar worthy Dev Patel) who must fight monsters he can and cannot see. It's a unique and unforgettable film that ranks with the year's best.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: A movie all about ideas, but it can't make those ideas cohere to the framework of a medieval romance.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: It's a movie that blends both fantastical and entertaining elements of a mainstream epic with something signature to its filmmaker's heart.
reviews.author: Soham Gadre

reviews.text: It's been over 40 years since Excalibur gave us a truly classic take on the Arthurian mythos, but David Lowery has given us a new one. Unfortunately it's not for the uninitiated; if medieval epics isn't your thing, you may wind up scratching your head.
reviews.author: Bill Watters

reviews.text: A visually stunning, cerebral dissection of the Messiah complex and its ties to monarchy.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: As the film stands, its quest feels more aimless than even Gawain at its open: a kind of aesthetic tourism that's only so productive.
reviews.author: George Elkind

reviews.text: I haven't stopped thinking about it.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: David Lowery's The Green Knight [is] a slog through Arthurian legend that possesses little of the meaning or formal rigor of the director's previous work.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: A very unique and welcome cinematic experience.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: The whole dreamy rendering is rooted but simultaneously airy, a lofty lore, freakishly forged by visionary filmmaking.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Lowery's latest, a surprisingly playful yet at times severe retelling of an old tale brought anew, is an assured triumph. The Green Knight is one of the year's best films.
reviews.author: Allyson Johnson

reviews.text: The Green Knight finally lets Arthurian legend get weird, and with it comes a masterfully atmospheric journey that won't be for everyone, but for those that can get on its level, it'll become a new favorite.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: Those who wish to attain the state of chastity in spiritual enlightenment must strive to become green knights-the complimentary color, and polar opposite color, of lustful red. Fantastic revelation. Just wish the tale had been told more engagingly.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: There's an illusive quality to "The Green Knight," which is Lowery's intent. It's a film that requires multiple viewings in order to absorb all it has to say and appreciate the artistry it contains.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: While The Green Knight will disappoint those seeking big-screen adventure, its mesmerizing oddness ensures it won't soon be forgotten.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Those looking for a film that does full justice to the original tale may be disappointed by The Green Knight's lapse into a familiar story of a womanizing ne'er-do-well taught the true value of honor through his trials...
reviews.author: Colleen Morrissey

reviews.text: In "The Green Knight," Lowery revises a legend, in style and in substance, in order to evoke a way of telling different stories, and of telling stories differently.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: This is the kind of movie you get lost in for a little while.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Patel's explosive performance pushes this fever dream of a film into award-worthy contender territory.
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: With impeccable production design, gorgeous cinematography, and a leisurely pace that never bores, The Green Knight fulfills its aesthetic promise.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Well-cast with a rock-solid sense of self, a strangely endearing sense of humor, and a compelling lead, The Green Knight makes for one of 2021's unmissable (if utterly bizarre) summer flicks.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Rich with stunning visuals and intoxicating pacing, it provides a surreal coming-of-age chivalric romance that sets it apart from any prior medieval adaptation.
reviews.author: Sabrina Ramirez

reviews.text: The Green Knight -- an epic in miniature, a fantasy all the more poignant for its moral realities -- makes this a lesson worth learning.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: The Green Knight goes on a cinematic quest that for the viewer means finding more than mere entertainment.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Patel shows his talent, physically and emotionally, to take on this challenging role. Lowery presents suffering, violence, and sex in a haunting morality tale wrapped in an aesthetically elegant package.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: There is little irony or modernity on display, and Lowery's visual flourishes, along with his command of tone, helps us accept this unusual commitment to sincerity.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: I myself masked up and saw it on the big screen, and wouldn't have wanted to experience it any other way.
reviews.author: Taylor Antrim

reviews.text: From the ambitious set design, constant creative camera work, thought provoking scene structure, and hypnotic performances, The Green Knight excels despite it's polarizing nature.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: For those who delight in the manipulations of court politics... and the scourge of societal roles pushed upon those with no understanding of them, this is the deep-cut spooky Arthurian art house film they only dreamed might one day exist.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: You can't touch it. You can't feel it, or really even get near it. But it sure does look pretty from afar.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: An adult-oriented challenge to conventional fantasy thrills, David Lowery's complex, puzzling, and visually triumphant 'The Green Knight' leans into onscreen natural horrors and sexual proclivities to tell the story of a knight of faltering courage
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: The Green Knight has its share of flaws but there's a freshness to Lowery's approach that demands to be noticed.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: With all the gushing cinematic pomp and circumstance, Lowery's film is a simple game of truth AND dare. Well, I'd rather not play, but I'll watch.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: Like Peter Brook's stage and film adaptations of the [Mahabharata], the multi-cultural casting works hand in hand with this story's universal themes.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: That's part of what gives the film its hypnotic vibe in creating indelible visuals and moments that sear into your memory.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: "The Green Knight" does not look, feel or play like a summer movie because it enthralls more than entertains in the visually ambitious hands of director/screenwriter David Lowery.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: The Green Knight works its magic to a degree
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: Beautiful in spite of the subtle rot woven throughout, Lowery's England is a quiet nightmare as often as it is a wondrous dream.
reviews.author: Aly Caviness

reviews.text: This movie could use a good dragon...
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: There are oohs and aahs in the film, as Lowery creates an Arthurian moodiness ... & is that Merlin? W/magic, mystery and a perfectly stunning ending that satisfies in every way.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: This movie has such an energy to it, your attention is commanded throughout. And I felt very convinced that Dev Patel is a movie star.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: The Green Knight is an excellent adaptation, filled with phantasmagoric imagery and buoyed by an ever-present feeling of dread...the kind of artistic endeavor that will entice audiences into the theater, then fully divide them by the final frame.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: It's a gorgeous movie, and it has some really nice elements to it. But it's not for everyone, and it can be challenging at times.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: This is an unlikely and unconventional film that represents a career-high for David Lowery.
reviews.author: Dave Platt

reviews.text: Patel provides the humanity that anchors the dreamlike, sometimes surreal images that Lowery produces, a dose of old-soul wisdom that makes "The Green Knight" a story for the ages.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The Green Knight is lavishly realized but strangely hollow.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: David Lowery's latest is a mesmerizing medieval fantasy.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: A dazzling, dizzying fever dream...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: You need to be comfortable with that feeling to go along with Green Knight. For the most part, I was and I did.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Lowery never needed to convince audiences that Gawain was worthy; Patel did all that himself, extracting the dignity that was within Gawain from the beginning.
reviews.author: Tyler Bey

reviews.text: With David Lowery behind the camera, this is your freshman English class on mushrooms. It's not a bad trip.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: Jade Healy's production design and Malgosia Turzanska's costume design are marvelously imaginative and Oscar-worthy, stunningly photographed by cinematographer Andrew Droz Palermo.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: David Lowery makes movies that make me feel like I'm watching a movie for the first time.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: A visually and sonically gorgeous film, featuring a dynamite lead performance by Patel, a stunning production design by Jade Healy, and one of the year's best scores, by Daniel Hart.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Patient, open-minded viewers will know they've seen something at the end of this slow, exasperatingly fussy movie
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: David Lowery's movie, starring Dev Patel, cleverly unfolds the public consequences of private indiscretions.
reviews.author: Jo Livingstone

reviews.text: There is something magically entrancing about this fantastical Arthurian tale of a recklessly brave knight, played by Dev Patel in a career best role
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: The Green Knight transforms a 14th Medieval poem into a gorgeous piece of cinema art.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: Indeed, Lowery doesn't seem interested in a straightforward, realistic adaptation so much as creating a vibe.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: [A] haunting epic - dark, dreamy, and worthy of King Arthur's court.
reviews.author: Kimberley Elizabeth

reviews.text: Moody, slow-moving and existential, The Green Knight is gorgeous but dense -- what you might get if Terrence Malick decided to make a Knights of the Round Table movie.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Lowery's blockbuster-agnostic approach to [The Green Knight] is never less than confident, [but] consistent mood and succinct spectacle are not where his strengths ultimately lie.
reviews.author: Michael Scoular

reviews.text: 'The Green Knight' is overflowing with curious, well-inked text located between the lines. Some will recognize the film's beauty quickly, while others may dismiss it as weird nonsense or acknowledge it later.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Monty Python and the Holy Grail and Lancelot du Lac have had a baby.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: The film seizes Lowery's best skills as a director: his eye for innocence and nature and how he uses slowness to deepen a story.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: David Lowery's The Green Knight is...a haunting, confounding, surprisingly erotic fantasy epic; a confrontation between man and nature, nature and religion, man and himself.
reviews.author: Brianna Zigler

reviews.text: "The Green Knight" wields a peculiar magic, the reason being that Lowery-as he showed in "A Ghost Story," which ranged with ease over centuries-is consumed by cinema's capacity to measure and manipulate time.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: For those so inclined, The Green Knight is divine, literally and figuratively. It is a triumphant, boldly serious, carefully modernized take on an archaic but still relevant ode to not being a dickweed. English majors, rejoice responsibly.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: The film wrestles with every step of this journey, emphasizing Gawain's humanity over his humility.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: ...about the very idea of legends: how they grow, what they reveal, what they conceal.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: If Terrence Malick (Tree of Life) directed Game of Thrones, it might look something like this.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: A haunting, richly-layered retelling of the classic Arthurian legend with a unique creative vision that's true to writer / director David Lowery.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Lowery laces his movie with imagery both beautiful and horrific, all of it rapturously filmed, while bringing his own sensibilities to the familiar milieu.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: The Green Knight is undoubtedly beautiful. ... It is equally undoubtedly weird.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The Green Knight is stunning. Featuring the absolute best cinematography of the year, this slowly paced film takes a few turns that will have viewers mesmerized.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Often fluttering between reality and a dreamlike existence and embracing the mystical elements of its source material, The Green Knight revels in its own ambiguity.
reviews.author: Michelle Jaworski

reviews.text: The Green Knight is, simply, not home screen material. To witness...David Lowery's epic...on anything other than the largest screen possible would be like reducing the Grand Canyon to a postcard; the Sistine Chapel to a page in a coloring book.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: The Green Knight is supposed to be a tale about what it means to be human; Lowery's film is entirely void of that humanity.
reviews.author: Juan Barquin

reviews.text: An epic meal of a film, David Lowery's "The Green Knight" unspools its vast scope in one transfixing two hour mediation.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Fraught with gorgeous cinematography, steady pacing, and a commanding performance by Dev Patel, The Green Knight comes to life in glorious detail.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: It's one of the most dazzlingly strange films I've seen in ages, and one of my favorites of the year so far.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: The Green Knight's retelling of the classic fourteenth century poem is dense, deliberate and often beautiful. But just as often it is willfully obtuse as it gets lost in the surreal deconstruction of Gawain's journey.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: In virtually every scene, Patel is simply marvelous.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Every film is going to be a kind of reflection of its creator, but a creator without empathy can only hope to create a mirror, and even an incredible actor like Patel can't overcome this.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: This version of The Green Knight also does right by its women, giving Alicia Vikander a fair amount to do as both Gawain's earnest love interest Esel and her doppelgänger.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: The chapters don't cohere in a sustained rhythm, but in richly evocative imagery, "The Green Knight" makes its own vivid film language and pacing.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: The Arthurian myths remain because we come to them, not because we reshape them, and they are open to all. In this realization, The Green Knight is the stuff of pure mythos.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: In writer/director Lowery's hands, this well-worn story that's been around for literal centuries becomes something extraordinarily original...
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: Countless shots look as if they were painted directly into a medieval storybook. The film's aesthetic is a mixture of wonder and darkness that feels like it taps into the very origins of fantasy as a genre.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: A visual stunner from start to finish, but The Green Knight does slip into frustratingly enigmatic territory before rebounding strong and sticking the landing with one of the most breathtaking sequences of the year.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: It's an incoherent mood piece, a jumble of themes and ideas that never coagulates into anything of substance...In other words, it's the perfect vessel for film critics to laud as "high art,"
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: A bona fide masterpiece, wrapping dreams of heroism and chivalry in a cloak of otherworldly horror that slowly tightens around your throat until you can scarcely breathe.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: Suffice it to say that this tale, romantic and symbolic in equal measure, ends exactly and breathtakingly as it must.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: It's not everyday that you watch a film that appears to be rewriting the cinematic language to create something you've never seen before, but David Lowery achieves just that with this Arthurian masterpiece. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario Alegre

reviews.text: As an experience of mood, tone, style and atmosphere, it's right up there with A24's Hereditary and The Lighthouse, a nightmare forged in blood, guts, myth, mist and mystery.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: Many movies have been made around the legend of King Arthur and his knights, but none quite like this unusual, entrancing adventure, with its dreamlike touches, stirring movements, and quiet poetry.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: The Green Knight joins Excalibur as a film that deftly explores the Arthurian universe.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: Dev Patel shines in David Lowery's evocative and allegorical interpretation of The Green Knight.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Lowery dives all the way in and viewers are rewarded with a sumptuous feast for the eyes and the soul.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: It's an elusive film, in its plotting and allusions, but is still potent and immediate, as resonant as any of our own late-night quests toward the far reaches of our self-conception.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: As a parable of greed and consequence, The Green Knight delivers compelling drama, even as we're not always sure where it's headed (which is not necessarily a negative).
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Lowery has taken a young man's journey of self-discovery and fashioned it into a gorgeous and moving work of art.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: There are more serious currents, but it's also a gnarly dorm-poster movie full of weird creatures, color-blocked psych-outs, and horny Alicia Vikanders.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: Leaning into the Pagan roots of the story, The Green Knight keeps its story on the side of the beautiful and terrible.
reviews.author: Shelagh Rowan-Legg

reviews.text: The weirdness of Lowery's vision might be frighteningly unfamiliar, but it's probably the way to adapt a text that's more than 600 years old, imparting a primal force to this legendary tale.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: "The Green Knight" initially finds Sir Gawain a bold young man with no tales to tell. The knight we leave has one worth experiencing multiple times.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Never has chivalric romance and so-called adventure been treated so pensively.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: [Lowery] is basically the perfect filmmaker for this material, leading us into a labyrinth of essential questions about the nature of time, of purpose, of existence, in an unhurried but visually dynamic (and then some) way.
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Occupying practically every scene, Patel makes a striking and relatable hero, spending much of the time as confused as the audience is apt to be.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Many of the images will certainly have staying power and it is a film that is begging for multiple re-watches, as it is densely layered and there is a lot to unpack. While its mass appeal is probably limited, those who love it are going to really love it.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: "...the next great film in the modern fantasy canon, one we should be talking about for decades to come."
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: The Green Knight is a heart-rattling, loins-riling, and head-spinning trip that packs a profound punch.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: The finest fantasy film in decades.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: The Green Knight feels like an anachronistic oddity -- a film from and of another time and another world.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: "The Green Knight" is a stunner, every bit the must-see event A24's often exaggerated PR promised it would be.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: The Green Knight is an impressive collision between two sensibilities that doesn't always work but remains curious and will haunt audiences' minds for a long time.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: This movie is worth watching twice.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: "The Green Knight" casts a magical, and sometimes mist-bound, spell.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: You don't get the sense that Lowery hates the genre he's working in. Instead, you just get the sense that he's going through the motions, too caught up in the imagery to nurse the characters or the ideas.
reviews.author: Hunter Lanier

reviews.text: The freedom that Lowery assumes for himself is staggering - and encouraging. "The Green Knight" is artistically from Jupiter, except that its real source resides deep in the human soul.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Cinematic poetry and one of the most visually resplendent films of the year.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The characters are so unsympathetic and abnormal and illogical that the story steadily deteriorates into less and less satisfying visions of fantastical esotericism.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Patel transcends with his incredible character arc and depth of emotions brought on by internal struggles. It's a truly Oscar worthy performance.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: A dark, visually mesmerizing fantasy that embellishes the poem's concise narrative with episodes that expand intelligently on its essential themes.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Birthed from the epic poem of Sir Gawain and the Green Knight, the film is a patient, visually pleasing heroic tale that blends Celtic mythology and Christian faith. It also provides a truly mythical, seductive spin on the familiar Camelot.
reviews.author: Adriana Gomez-Weston

reviews.text: A breathtaking, cerebral and exhilarating experience brimming with visual poetry. Like all truly great films, it transcends words. Dev Patel gives the best performance of his career.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: The Green Knight brings an unconventional horror spin on the King Arthur legends by putting more emphasis on the human mind and spirit experiencing terror rather than on elaborate and bloody physical battles.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: A methodical, if largely allegorical, exploration of its main character's psyche, the film smooths out the enduring mysteries, opaque psychology, and narrative idiosyncrasies of its source material.
reviews.author: Keith Watson

reviews.text: The Green Knight invites the viewer to lose their way in a truly unfamiliar world, and thereby learn something of themselves.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: Pretty much a masterpiece -- an audacious and often mesmerizing work that takes familiar narrative tropes and makes them feel thrillingly new in the most unexpected and exhilarating of ways.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Thank god (or gods?) for David Lowery.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: It's the movie Lowery was born to make, a dreamy piece of high fantasy that bombards the viewer with visual delights, skimps on all but the most essential dialogue, and turns an age-old tale into something to be puzzled over anew.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Looking at it is like being immersed in a medieval tapestry. Watching it is like being immersed in a Jungian dream filled with choices, enigmatic patterns and symbols.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Moviegoers who are familiar with the source material for "The Green Knight" might find it a thought-provoking, updated take on the ancient poem.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: It doesn't feel like a movie for the present, nor does it feel like something unearthed from the past. It feels like a fairy tale.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Delivered at a deliberate pace, with a build towards the fantastical, this A24 epic does plenty to impress.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Rather than tease a particular reading out of Gawain's journey, the beguiling work functions as a meditation on the search for meaning and direction itself.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: The Green Knight is a piece of art, a pristine wonder of storytelling being brought to life, and leaving us to think about what it all meant.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Those willing to surrender to its talking animals, to its fevered surrealness, and to its Old World myth-weaving will be thoroughly rewarded with one of the year's best films.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: David Lowery continues to impress with this gloomy, heady and entrancing exploration of honor, love and destiny. A unique experience without a doubt. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: The Green Knight is a feast for the eyes, the senses, the mind, and the soul.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: The Green Knight tells an enthrallingly hypnotic cautionary tale about honor, packed with some of the most potent acting and craftsmanship likely to be seen in a film all year
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: A movie that's both of its time and splendidly out of step with it, an act of necromancy in a CGI world.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: The film is a slow, mournful rumination on our desires to live forever through story, song, and deed -- a fitting adaptation from the director of A Ghost Story, another movie deeply interested in facing death head-on.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: The Green Knight is both a student of the past and a well-meaning raider of it; this is a film which will honor a story J.R.R. Tolkien singled out as one of the greatest works of English literature, as well as gracefully deconstruct it.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: Here's a story that's so inherently loose and extemporaneous. It doesn't help, then, that [the] approach is hermetic enough that there's not too much of the film from its neck up.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: The Green Knight is not a film that washes over you, it strikes you in the chest and drags you under - and, believe me, you will surrender happily.
reviews.author: Caitlin Kennedy

reviews.text: An enormous epic, a truly cinematic voyage that pulls you further in as it goes along, and doesn't give you a moment to even want it to let up.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The Green Knight has a lot of religious undertones but the film remains Loweryian in nature.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: 'The Green Knight' oozes Arthurian style on a more intimate, visually hypnotic level akin to A24's slow-and-stunning signatures, and while it undoubtedly feels its length, does showcase David Lowery's keen directorial eye with the right spotlight.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: The Green Knight is going to delight a lot of cinephiles, especially those who have been looking forward to it for a year. It's also going to frustrate mainstream moviegoers.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Led by Dev Patel at his most magnetic, this is a fantastical adventure in a genre all of its own.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: It's no surprise that greatness in cinema, as in Gawain's story, comes from patience, attention, and imagination. The result is truly legendary.
reviews.author: Proma Khosla

reviews.text: Lowery's unforgettable adaptation refuses to do the math for us, but it's all the more thrilling for how it insists that the only true value of a thing in this world is that which we find in it for ourselves.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Those expecting an Arthurian sword-and-sandals battle epic will be sorely disappointed. Instead, Lowery has delivered a dense, sensual, almost dream-like tale of chivalry, magic, temptation and transformation.
reviews.author: Brandon Katz

reviews.text: The movie's more ruminative than exuberant. It's also fully invested in making its own kind of magic, on its own time.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: [A] mesmerizing journey guided by Lowery's incredibly poetic eye, career-best work from Dev Patel, and an artistic sensibility that transports audiences to another world.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: If you're willing to go with Lowery and his vision, The Green Knight is a rewarding, resonant journey with wonderful performances and some things you've never seen before.
reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

reviews.text: Fans of epic tales like Lord of the Rings will find themselves transfixed with this intelligent and thought-provoking trip back to that time.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: A beautiful, haunting and enigmatic work that reckons with the folklore's grave and tragic elements to deliver a masterpiece of blood, sex and magic.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: While there's a lot of commendable chutzpah and curious longing baked into The Green Knight, the movie's never as compelling as it is unusual.
reviews.author: Simon Abrams

reviews.text: Lowery's The Green Knight is cinema's best Arthurian adaptation, which may matter only to literary scholars. Everyone else will have to settle for it being one of the best movies of 2021.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: To disguise a film so artful and boldly uncommercial as mass-market entertainment for those still hurting from Game of Thrones' conclusion - there's your act of heroism.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: With lush visuals, a strong star turn from Dev Patel and some thoughtful ruminations on Hollywood heroism and masculinity, David Lowery' 'The Green Knight' is about as good as you hoped.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: It boldly reimagines one of the most famous Arthurian tales, and in doing so feels like a relic from an ancient era when the barrier was thin between the world of men and the world of magic, mystery, and everything green.
reviews.author: Emma Stefansky

reviews.text: Several heads roll though it's your mind that'll get truly blown by "The Green Knight," a visually dazzling and thoughtful trip back to Camelot.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: I got caught up in it (to a point). I was, in the end, moved by it. I was also, at moments, slightly baffled by it. But I saw how it added up, and I was glad to go with it.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: A spectacle of contradictions: as grandiose as the canon of tales to which it belongs but also oddly intimate in focus, with a modern psychology that clashes productively with its squalid evocation of the far bygone yesteryear.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Lowery's latest impresses and wows with a tactile, beguiling dark fantasy epic that cuts right to the Pagan heart of Arthurian legend.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: David Lowery threads the needle between existential and linear storytelling, making for a hypnotic, challenging, and visually lush experience.
reviews.author: Patrick Cavanaugh

reviews.text: From the opening frame to its final shot, The Green Knight is a visual masterpiece.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: In The Green Knight, the infinite mysteries of the natural world are reframed in an Arthurian retelling so strange and so seductive that...it burrows underneath your skin.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: The Green Knight is all at once thrilling, gorgeous, and haunting
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Told in sumptuously gritty imagery, this epic feat of bold imagination is unconcerned with mitigating its creative force for the sake of unadventurous audiences.
reviews.author: Carlos Aguilar

reviews.text: The Green Knight is the culmination of a decade's worth of entertaining, thought provoking work coming together to create a defining achievement within Lowery's career.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

synopsis: An epic fantasy adventure based on the timeless Arthurian legend, THE GREEN KNIGHT tells the story of Sir Gawain (Dev Patel), King Arthur's reckless and headstrong nephew, who embarks on a daring quest to confront the eponymous Green Knight, a gigantic emerald-skinned stranger and tester of men. Gawain contends with ghosts, giants, thieves, and schemers in what becomes a deeper journey to define his character and prove his worth in the eyes of his family and kingdom by facing the ultimate challenger. From visionary filmmaker David Lowery comes a fresh and bold spin on a classic tale from the knights of the round table.
